purpose: Test whether professional capability plus fragmented/flexible time is itself an unorganized missing edge before spending field-access effort.

current_market_evidence.evidence: Current Xuzhou recruitment results include part-time CPA roles and multiple accounting roles explicitly marked flexible or part-time, including day-rate work.
current_market_evidence.implication: Professional accounting capacity already has visible market routes; generic fractional accounting is not a defensible missing edge.

current_market_evidence.evidence: Current Xuzhou-targeted listings include part-time interior/design work described as no fixed office, online coordination, work from home and payment per order.
current_market_evidence.implication: Outcome-like remote design exchange already exists in ordinary recruitment markets.

current_market_evidence.evidence: Current Xuzhou-targeted listings include home-based part-time data-analysis work and part-time new-media operations.
current_market_evidence.implication: Fragmented-time professional work is not absent as a category.

current_market_evidence.evidence: Current local recruitment systems expose a dedicated gig market and professional part-time categories such as accounting, design, legal, translation and IT/software.
current_market_evidence.implication: A new generic marketplace or matching layer would duplicate already-visible discovery routes.

decision.reason: The broad professional-flexibility exchange is already materially organized by existing recruitment/gig routes. Remaining value, if any, must be evidenced as a repeated failure mode after those routes, not inferred from caregiver time constraints or professional capability alone.

reopen_only_if: multiple capability-side actors with verifiable prior professional skills report the same material failure after trying current part-time, remote or freelance routes
multiple small operators report the same bounded professional outcome remains undone after considering current hiring, gig and agency routes
the failure is caused by a specific missing edge such as trust, acceptance design, coordination shape, liability allocation or time granularity rather than lack of listings
at least one outcome class can be accepted objectively and paid fairly without relying on constrained workers accepting discounted compensation
coordination cost stays below created surplus
kill_if: the only differentiation is branding the same part-time/freelance work around caregivers
the route merely aggregates listings already available on recruitment or gig platforms
the task class is already routinely bought per order or per day through existing channels
economics require underpayment or hidden unpaid coordination
no repeated post-platform failure appears in direct actor evidence
